explanation: `LinearMap.coe_domRestrict` (Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Submodule/LinearMap.lean, line 150) states the identical equation `⇑(f.domRestrict p) = Set.domRestrict p f`, but for a semilinear map `f : M →ₛₗ[σ₁₂] M₂`. The target is the continuous version: it follows by instantiating that lemma with the underlying semilinear map `f.toLinearMap` of the given continuous linear map. Since `ContinuousLinearMap.domRestrict f p` is `f ∘SL p.subtypeL`, whose underlying linear map is definitionally `f.toLinearMap.comp p.subtype` (`Submodule.subtypeL` has `toLinearMap := p.subtype`, `ContinuousLinearMap.comp` is defined via `LinearMap.comp`), and since `Set.domRestrict p f = fun x ↦ f x`, both sides are definitionally the same function as in the LinearMap statement; hence a single application closes the goal (`exact`/`simpa` up to unfolding of `domRestrict`, `comp`, `subtypeL`). It is not a full duplicate because the object (continuous linear map vs. linear map) and hence the type of the statement differ, so the linear-map lemma must be instantiated to a specific function (`f.toLinearMap`). The library's current proof is just `rfl`.
